title: Counselor Desk Guidance on Recent Defaults and the Patient Payment Plans Tiers Offered
content:
Under the Patient Payment Plans, a patient's plan history across all of the patient's plans limits which tiers may be offered.

**The rule the desk applies.** A tier whose prior-default lockout is above 0 is not offered while the patient has a recent default; tiers with no lockout remain available.

**What counts as a recent default.** The count of the patient's other payment plans with a default date inside a rolling window of the tier's prior-default lockout, in calendar months, ending on the handling date. A plan counts whether or not it was later reinstated. A patient has a recent default for that tier when the count is 1 or more.

**Reinstatement and payoff do not clear it.** The tier stays unavailable even if the earlier plan was later reinstated and paid off.

**Tiers that remain open.** Because tiers with no lockout remain available, a patient with a recent default may still be offered the 3-Month or 6-Month Interest-Free Plan (within their balance ranges) or, with a current hardship approval, the Financial Hardship Plan.

### Decision table

A tier is offered, as far as this rule goes, exactly when its lockout is 0 or the count of recent defaults for that tier is 0:

| Tier's prior-default lockout | Plans with a default date inside the lockout window | Tier offered under this rule |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | Yes |
| 0 | 1 or more | Yes |
| Above 0 | 0 | Yes |
| Above 0 | 1 or more | No |

### Worked situations (hypothetical dates)

- A patient's earlier plan defaulted 10 calendar months before the handling date, was reinstated and was then paid off. For a tier with a lockout above 10 months, the default date falls inside the window; the count is 1 and the tier is not offered. For a tier with no lockout, the tier remains available.
- The window is measured separately for each tier with its own lockout length: a default date that falls inside a longer lockout window can fall outside a shorter one, and the tier with the shorter window is then offered as far as this rule goes.
